bib.title: Aggregation of Reasoning: A Hierarchical Framework for Enhancing Answer Selection in Large Language Models

question: When an LLM can generate the correct answer among sampled reasoning chains but wrong answers are more frequent, how can the right one be selected?
hypothesis: Evaluating the reasoning chains themselves, not just answer frequency, selects the correct answer more often than majority voting.
contributions: Show that frequency-based ensembling is insufficient and design AoR, a hierarchical aggregation of reasoning chains
Use evaluation scores of the best chains to sample dynamically and cut overhead
Show better performance and cost efficiency than existing ensemble methods

method.summary: AoR samples CoT chains, buckets them by answer, has an LLM score chains within each bucket (local scoring), then jointly scores the top chains of different buckets (global evaluation, k rounds) and picks the bucket with highest mean score. Dynamic sampling adds chains in batches while the top-two score margin is below a threshold.
method.task: reasoning answer selection / chain ensembling (math, commonsense, symbolic)

inference.temperature: 1 for GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-4, Claude-2; 0.6 for LLaMA-2; 0.7 for Mistral
inference.samples: AoR(20,40): 20 initial chains, dynamic sampling to nmax=40; baselines 40 chains; at most 500 samples per analysis run; single run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: Few-shot CoT exemplars from Wei et al. 2022 and Fu et al. 2023 (3 to 8 per dataset); scoring prompts with 4 criteria (10 points) plus manual demonstrations, and statistics (chains per bucket, number of candidate answers) in the prompt

parameters.local criteria: Logical Consistency 3, Appropriateness of Method 3, Completeness and Clarity 2, Application of Knowledge 2
parameters.global criteria: Validity of Approach 3, Consistency of Steps and Answer 3, Completeness and Clarity 2, Application of Knowledge 2
parameters.new-chain benchmark: best and worst chain in same answer bucket as demonstrations

other.cost formula: Input Tokens x 0.0015/1000 + Output Tokens x 0.002/1000
other.experiment dates: main July to September 2023; discussion October to December 2023

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: Regex extract after 'the answer is', compare numerically, by option, or yes/no; chains with no extractable answer are dropped

eval.protocol: Single run per setting as far as stated; no seeds or significance tests stated. ComplexCoT and ComplexCoT-PHP numbers taken from Zheng et al. 2023. DiVeRSe verifiers fine-tuned per task.

limits: Relies on manually written demonstrations so the evaluator emits scores in a parseable format; unstable if the model deviates
Context window limits how many chains can be scored together; small models can score only single chains, raising cost
Main experiments use GPT-3.5-Turbo-0301 only; single run, no variance or significance reported; at most 500 samples per analysis
Evaluator is the same LLM family as the generator, scoring quality rests on LLM self-judgment; GPT-4 evaluator helps
Full prompts are in a GitHub repo, not the paper; dated 2023 models and pre-reasoning-model methods

terms.definition: Aggregation of Reasoning: hierarchical framework with local-scoring, global-evaluation and dynamic sampling
chains yielding identical answers are scored on soundness of reasoning; top k above threshold epsilon kept
top chains from different answer buckets are jointly scored; bucket with highest mean score over k rounds wins
